title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product teams involved in detecting, mitigating, and communicating incidents. The document includes: incident severity taxonomy, paging and escalation, runbook structure and examples, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation guidance, game day best practices, status page rules, and customer communication templates.

Table of contents:
1) Incident taxonomy & SLOs
2) Pager & escalation flow
3) Runbook standard and example
4) Immediate incident checklist (first 30 minutes)
5) Postmortem and RCA requirements
6) On-call rotations & handoff
7) Game day playbook
8) Status page rules
9) Customer communication templates
10) Ownership & related pages

1) Incident taxonomy & SLOs
- Severity levels (applies to public-facing services and internal infra):
  - Sev 1 (P0): Full service outage or severe degradation impacting >25% of requests, violating critical SLOs (availability or latency) and causing widespread customer impact.
  - Sev 2 (P1): Significant partial outage or degraded performance affecting a subset of customers or features; SLOs degraded but system partially functional.
  - Sev 3 (P2): Non-urgent bug, performance regression with limited customer impact, or background job failures.
  - Sev 4 (P3): Minor issues, documentation errors, or feature requests.

- Representative SLOs (reference: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets):
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted API endpoints.
  - P50/P95/P99 latencies published per model route (targets vary by route; example: P95 < 300ms for small models).
  - Embedding throughput and error rate targets per contract for Dedicated customers.

2) Pager & escalation flow
- Alerting sources: Prometheus alerts, synthetic checks, logs (error rates), on-call phone/SMS, and customer support tickets escalated to on-call.
- Primary on-call: Responsible for initial triage and mitigation.
- Secondary on-call (escalation): Engaged if the primary cannot mitigate within the time-to-escalate thresholds.
- Time-to-escalate thresholds (guideline):
  - Sev 1: 5 minutes to acknowledge, 15 minutes to escalate to next responder if no progress.
  - Sev 2: 15 minutes to acknowledge, 60 minutes to escalate.
  - Sev 3+: follow team SLAs and log in the incident tracker.

Escalation path (example):
1. Pager -> Primary on-call (service owner).
2. If no ack or insufficient progress -> Secondary on-call (team lead/SRE).
3. If cross-service impact -> Platform SRE pager and on-call manager.
4. For customer-impacting outages with billing/contract implications -> Notify Customer Success and Sales engineering.

Contact list (maintain in team roster):
- Primary on-call: team-specific entry
- Secondary on-call: team-specific entry
- Platform SRE pager: +1-555-0100 (internal) / pager-slack #sre-pager
- Incident commander (IC): assigned per-incident

3) Runbook standard and example
- Every production service must have a concise runbook with:
  - Runbook name and owner_team
  - Pager rules and alert definitions (Prometheus or alerting query)
  - Quick triage checklist (first 5 checks)
  - Mitigation steps with rollback commands and safety checks
  - Verification steps and expected indicators of success
  - Post-incident follow-ups and links to dashboards

Runbook quick-check template (must be copyable into an ops page):
- Runbook: service-name runtime API
- Owner: infra-team
- Pager: prom-alert-id
- 0) Confirm alert: check prom query and dashboards (link)
- 1) Check core metrics: error rate, latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth
- 2) If controller pod crashed: kubectl -n svc get pods --selector=app=svc | grep CrashLoop
- 3) If GPU OOMs: inspect logs /var/log/runtime/gpu-oom.log; reduce batch size or restart node via autoscaler playbook
- 4) Hotfix (if safe): revert last deploy (git tag -> kubectl rollout undo) or scale replicas to X
- 5) Verification: synthetic request success, error rate back to baseline, latency within SLO

Example runbook table (as text):
| Step | Command / Action | Owner | Expected result | Rollback / Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Check error rate | Open dashboard /prom/query?srv=svc | Primary | error_rate < 1% | If >5%, escalate |
| Restart controller | kubectl rollout restart deploy/controller | Primary | pods reach Ready | If fail, scale to 0 -> 3 |

4) Immediate incident checklist (first 30 minutes)
1. Acknowledge the pager and set incident channel (Slack) and incident document (Confluence incident page).
2. Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communication Lead, Scribe, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).
3. Triage and classify severity, add SLOs impacted to incident page.
4. Begin mitigation steps from runbook; log all commands and results in incident page.
5. Update status page and customer comms per status rules (see section 8).
6. If the incident is prolonged (>60 minutes for Sev1), schedule regular update cadence (every 15 minutes).

Role definitions:
- Incident Commander (IC): single decision owner for the incident. Coordinates triage and escalation, approves public communications and major rollbacks.
- Communication Lead: owns status updates (internal and external), drafts customer-facing messages, and coordinates with Customer Success.
- Scribe: records timeline, commands executed, and evidence for postmortem.
- SMEs: execute runbook steps and provide technical guidance.

5) Postmortem and RCA requirements
- Postmortem is required for all Sev1 and Sev2 incidents and for Sev3 if requested by the IC or manager.
- Postmortem content must include:
  - Title, severity, incident ID, incident start and end times
  - Summary (TL;DR) of customer impact and root cause
  - Timeline of events (minute-granularity for first 60 minutes, then 5-15 minute granularity)
  - Root cause analysis (avoid blame; focus on facts)
  - Corrective actions (short-term mitigations and long-term fixes), owners and due dates
  - Post-incident verification plan and monitoring changes
  - Customer-facing summary (for incidents with external impact)

Postmortem template (short):
- Title:
- Incident ID:
- Severity:
- Start / End:
- Impact summary:
- Timeline:
- Root cause:
- Corrective actions (owner, due date):
- Follow-ups and verification:

6) On-call rotations & handoff
- Rotation cadence: teams typically run 1-week rotations for primary on-call; SRE teams may use 2-week rotations depending on load.
- Handover procedure (each rotation change):
  1. Outgoing on-call posts final status summary to team channel and incident tracker.
  2. Outgoing on-call transfers any open incidents and ongoing mitigations to incoming on-call in a scheduled 30-minute handoff meeting.
  3. Update the on-call roster in the team wiki (email pager duty and Slack handle).
- Time off and escalations: on-call engineers should swap rotations via self-service (Slack integration). For extended absences, managers must assign a backup.
- On-call burn policy: limit to maximum of 1 week of on-call per calendar month for engineers on feature rotations; teams should monitor burn and adjust assignments.

7) Game days (regular exercises)
- Purpose: test runbooks, validate alerting, exercise cross-team coordination, and practise IC/communication roles.
- Frequency: teams run at least one game day per quarter for critical services; platform-wide game days twice per year.
- Game day structure:
  1. Define scenario and expected outcomes (owner creates a Confluence game-day page).
  2. Pre-game checklist: telemetry baseline, participant list, communication channels ready.
  3. Run exercise (30-90 minutes), collect metrics and timeline.
  4. Post-game review: publish findings and action items in a short report.

8) Status page rules
- Use the public status page for customer-visible incidents. Internal status pages may be used for internal comms.
- Update cadence: initial 'Investigating' update within 15 minutes of confirmation for Sev1/Sev2; follow-up cadence every 15 minutes until Mitigated, then every 1 hour during Recovery, and a final Resolved update when all verification is complete.
- Status page content must include: summary, affected components, customer impact, mitigation steps underway, ETA (if available), and next update time.
- Do not include internal logs, command outputs, or PII on the public status page.

Status page update template (short):
- Title: [Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Recovering / Resolved]
- Time:
- Summary:
- Impacted components:
- What we're doing:
- Next update: (time)

9) Customer communication templates
- Use the Communication Lead to adapt the templates below. Keep tone clear, apologetic, and actionable. Do not speculate on root cause.

Customer short update (initial):
Subject: Redwood Inference - Service Disruption (investigating)
Body:
We are currently investigating an issue impacting the Redwood Inference API for some customers. Our engineers are triaging the issue and we will provide an update by [time]. We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience. If you are experiencing critical business impact, please reply and we will prioritize.

Customer follow-up (mitigating):
Subject: Redwood Inference - Incident Update (mitigating)
Body:
We have identified the root cause as [high-level cause] and are actively applying mitigations. Customers may see intermittent errors or increased latency; we expect to have a mitigation in place by [ETA]. For customers on Dedicated/Private deployments, your account team has been notified.

Customer final communication (resolved):
Subject: Redwood Inference - Incident Resolved
Body:
The incident that began at [start time] has been resolved as of [end time]. Root cause: [brief non-technical summary]. Impact: [what customers saw]. Actions taken: [short list]. We will follow up with a post-incident report including corrective actions and timeline. We apologize for the disruption.

10) Ownership & related pages
- Incident owner: team that operates the affected service.
- Platform SRE: supports cross-service coordination and escalations.
- Customer Success: coordinates customer notifications and account-specific impact.
- Security: notified if incident involves data exposure or unauthorized access.

Related pages and resources:
- /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-incident-response-playbook-2026-03-04.json

Appendix: quick-check command snippets (examples)
- Check API health endpoint: curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/health
- Check pods: kubectl -n service get pods -l app=service-name
- Restart rollout: kubectl -n service rollout restart deploy/controller

Appendix: incident postmortem checklist (owners must complete within 7 days for Sev1/Sev2)
- Create postmortem page and link incident ID
- Populate timeline and attach logs/graphs
- Assign corrective actions with owners and due dates
- Schedule follow-up validation and close the postmortem after verification

Notes and revision history:
- 2026-02-15: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2026-03-31: published and aligned with SRE quarterly review; added game day frequency guidance (reviewers: Carlos Mendes, Priya Rao)

For questions or to request changes, contact the Platform SRE team via #sre-team on Slack or open a PR against team runbooks.
